required: maximum two tonal planes per material
strong negative space around arms, legs, weapons and accessories
consistent visual weight with the rest of the roster
forbidden: bloom, lens flare or realistic glow (any glow is a flat solid shape)

Could the character be animated using relatively few large shapes?
Is the design readable at thumbnail size?
Are the colors flat and intentionally separated?

shape.tank: wide blocky rectangles and a big shield shape
shape.bruiser: heavy trapezoids, oversized fists and shoulders
shape.fighter: balanced diagonals with one clear weapon line
shape.assassin: sharp triangles, long thin blades, a low coiled posture
shape.caster: flowing diamonds and a bright flat focus shape
shape.blaster: long straight lines and a bold wedge-shaped weapon
shape.controller: hexagons and wide arc gestures with tools hanging off the body
shape.support: soft rounded rectangles with an open palm and a visible kit
shape.enchanter: circles and stars around a charm, instrument or talisman

simplify: FIGURE: about 12 to 15 big shapes in total
OUTLINE: one thin, uniform-weight black line, no sketchy or variable-weight lines
SHADING: each material is one flat color plus at most one flat darker shadow shape; no shine, no soft shading, no rim light
FACE: minimal; eyes are two simple geometric shapes (almond, slit or dot) under one brow line, nose one angular line, mouth one line; no eyelashes, eye highlights, iris detail or skin shading
HAIR and FUR: two to four big solid pointed shapes, never strands, braids, curls or texture

FABRIC: large flat planes with straight or sharply angled edges and at most three big creases; no ragged hems, ribbon streamers, patterns, embroidery, trim bands, tassels, stitching, studs or rows of buckles
METAL and GEAR: plain solid shapes in flat grey, black or an assigned color; chains are one thick plain line; no engraving or gold shading
HANDS and FEET: simple blocky shapes
at most ONE repeated graphic symbol on the whole figure
clear negative space between limbs, prop and body
artDirection.never: photorealism, 3D or CGI, painterly or watercolor texture, detailed anime rendering, airbrushing, gradients, glow or bloom or lens flare (a glow is a flat solid shape), fabric texture, tiny decorations, individual hairs, realistic reflections, generic fantasy concept art

lore.logline: In the Cold War year of 1986, Moscow went on every frequency and announced that vampires exist. The panic became a war that tore down the old world's infrastructure and stunted its technology for decades. Humans, vampires and werewolves now live behind cordons under a fragile treaty enforced by their Mystics, who meet every three months at the Temple of Imhotep. Power is inherited only by those who survive the trials of the Mummy Sorcerer Thoth-Ra in the Black Pyramid; the rest of the Mystics' secrets are sold in blood. Now the Elders of all three tribes are dead, the Chieftains are not who they seem, and a generation of children with powers is about to inherit a world that looks like the Dark Ages lit by neon.

cast.name: Ezekiel
cast.notes: Agent of Ramuset. Father of Anna. Shared secrets with Sullivan. Allied with Vincent.
cast.role: The man on the human chair who answers to a god.

cast.name: Anna
cast.kit: Staff, smoke pellets and pouch, barbed whip, round shield, chest plate
cast.role: Feels what is about to happen to the people around her.

cast.name: Josh
cast.notes: Dating Anna. His father Daniel is a prisoner.
cast.kit: Armored arm guards, broadsword and sheath, oval shield, chest plate
cast.role: Carries the storm. Wants his father out of the Block.

cast.name: Tom
cast.kit: Diamond shield, chest plate, silver compass, silver telescope, arm-guard crossbow, silver and wood arrows, thigh quivers
cast.role: Sees what others hide. The youngest of the three humans.

cast.name: Daniel
cast.role: The reason Josh wants the prison opened.

cast.name: Franklin Stein
cast.notes: Built the sentry chips and the cyber-zombies.
cast.role: Made the Block's guards. Left a son behind.

cast.name: Kristoff
cast.role: Stein's last project. Nothing hurts him.

cast.name: Delilah
cast.role: Talks people into things with a look.

cast.name: Emma
cast.role: A six-year-old vampire who flies. Nobody expected a child.

cast.name: Erik
cast.notes: Father of Greta and Nicholias. Shauna was loyal to him.

cast.name: Greta
cast.role: Steps through the dark between one moment and the next.

cast.name: Vincent
cast.notes: Allied with Ezekiel. Carries a sun amulet.
cast.role: A werewolf who has chosen a human ally.

cast.name: Morgan
cast.role: A mutt: neither pack nor outsider. Does Vincent's errands.

cast.name: Ramuset
cast.notes: A Mummy god. Temple north of the Block.

cast.name: Thoth-Ra
cast.notes: Judges every chosen one. Takes the souls of those who fail.
cast.role: Runs the trials, keeps the forfeit souls on file.

human.text: The human colony. Chieftain, Senate and Elders. Nothing innate, so they win on nerve, wheels and salvage.

subs.roadwar: The convoys that connect the colony to the Block, the Temple of Imhotep and the south road. Their drivers escort Mystics.
subs.arcade: The colony's training clans. Competition is how the Senate finds talent.
subs.pirateradio: The colony's voice. They are the only ones who still remember the exact words of the Broadcast.
subs.mallguard: The seat of the Senate and the colony's police and envoys.

vampire.text: The vampire colony. High Priest, Counsel and Lords. Rule by aristocracy and style.

subs.chromecourt: The Counsel's households and their duelists. The nobility.
subs.neonnocturnes: The night clubs that double as barracks and information markets.
subs.nightwatch: Rooftop guards who patrol the borders and enforce the treaty line.
subs.coterie: The High Priest's spies and quiet knives.

were.place: The Pylon Coast and the Scrapwild
were.text: The werewolf colony and the clans that swore to the Pack. Alpha Wolf, Pack Leaders and Greys.

subs.wolf: The Pack itself: Erik's line and the war-bands.
subs.raccoon: Scavengers and fixers who keep the colony's salvage economy alive.
subs.crocodile: River-holders on the coast. Smugglers and matriarchs.
subs.capybara: The calm clans: healers and diplomats who sit at the Mystic meetings.
subs.raven: Oracles and scouts who watch the borders.
subs.octopus: Spies and engineers in the flooded harbors.
subs.moth: Light-keepers who tend the old signal towers.
subs.spider: Couriers and weavers who run the Pack's message lines.

ghost.text: The war dead who stayed in the machines. Neutral, and the only ones who remember the last day.

subs.deadair: Haunters of dead broadcast stations: the Broadcast's own echo.
subs.lastcall: Those who died celebrating the end of the world.
subs.lingerers: Bound to the roads and wards where they died.

undead.place: The Block, the Zombie Territories and the Black Pyramid
undead.text: Zombies, Dr. Stein's cybernetic zombie-hybrids, and the Mummy court of Thoth-Ra and Ramuset.

subs.deadzone: The Block's guards: Dr. Stein's modified, armored zombies. The line never breaks.
subs.laborunion: Unmodified zombies who keep working because nobody told them to stop.
subs.notaries: The Mummy's bureaucracy: the Soul Notaries who file the souls forfeited in the trials.
subs.sandkings: The Mummy court: Thoth-Ra's royal guard and Ramuset's embalmers at the Black Pyramid.

forest.text: The old folk of the green edge of the Zombie Territories. They kept to themselves when the world burned.

subs.culdesac: A suburb swallowed by woods, still keeping its rules.
subs.rootserver: Dryads who grew into a dead data center.
subs.basementgnomes: Fortified cellars under the colonies' ruins.
subs.hobneighbors: Small helpers who attach themselves to households and never leave.

eldritch.text: Not from here. The flood and the Broadcast's echo let the unmoored things up under the Static Spires. Outside the treaty.

subs.deepones: The drowned civilization under the Spires.
subs.migo: The alien technologists who read the Broadcast and keep answering it.
subs.shoggoths: Living flesh that got loose in the flood.
subs.elderthings: The first architects, remembered in the pyramids.
subs.nightgaunts: Hunters in the dark between the colonies.
subs.hounds: Things that come through the sharp angles of time.

magic.place: Every colony, and the Black Pyramid
magic.text: The Mystic tradition. Four ways to hold the power that Thoth-Ra grants and the power some are simply born with.

subs.wizard: The academic Mystics: Elders and Lords who study what the trials teach.
subs.witch: The naturalist Mystics: Greys and wild practitioners who cultivate it.
subs.warlock: Those who bargained: the failed, the bound and the oathbreakers.
subs.mage: The born conduits: the generation now waking with powers.

threads.text: All nine Mystic Elders of all three tribes are dead, and Sullivan shared secrets with Ezekiel first. The chairs they left are held by Chieftains who benefit.
Ezekiel is his agent and controls scarabs. If every ascended leader passed Thoth-Ra's trial, how many are his?

threads.q: Why is Daniel in the Block?
threads.text: No one is released from the Block, and Josh knows it. What did his father do?
A human Elder married a vampire Lord, in a world where nobody crosses borders. What happened to their family, and is Tom connected to both?
Dr. Stein's son is invulnerable. Was he built to protect a secret, or to carry one?

threads.q: Why is a werewolf allied with a human Chieftain?
threads.text: Vincent wears a sun amulet and sends Morgan to run his errands. Who benefits from this alliance?
Emma is younger than the Cordon years suggest she should be. Are vampires being born again?
Something is still transmitting. The Mi-Go and the Dead Air stations both hear it.
In under three months the Mystics gather at the Temple of Imhotep, and there are almost no Mystics left to attend.

peoples.name: Human

peoples.tagline: No fangs, no fur. Just chrome, nerve and a very loud stereo.

peoples.name: Vampire
peoples.scene: a gutted skyscraper rooftop at night: a chandelier wired to car batteries, a dead neon sign, gothic antenna spires, a distant ruined skyline, rain
peoples.tagline: Glam, patient and very hard to kill.

peoples.name: Were-Creature
peoples.scene: a scrapyard war-den of rusted buses and tire-wall palisades, campfire barrels, hand-painted war totems, signal horns on tall poles

peoples.name: Ghost
peoples.scene: a dead broadcast station: racks of dark CRT monitors, cables drooping like willow branches, one flickering test-pattern screen, drifting fog

peoples.name: Undead
peoples.scene: a buried bunker vault and ash trench: steel blast doors, sandbag walls, a long corridor of lockers, dust-lit ventilation shafts
peoples.tagline: Not dead. Just on a very long shift.

peoples.name: Forest Spirit
peoples.scene: a drowned suburb overtaken by forest: roots through a server room, mossy satellite dishes, ferns on car roofs, low mist
peoples.tagline: The woods have opinions. They also have weapons.

peoples.name: Eldritch
peoples.scene: a flooded subway cathedral beneath the ruins: impossible angled architecture, sunken escalators, a dead monolith of glowing glyphs, rising black water, wrong geometry in the walls
peoples.tagline: Not from here. Not from now. Armed anyway.

peoples.name: Magic
peoples.scene: a ruined broadcast-and-ritual precinct: a leaning radio-tower observatory, a mushroom-furred factory floor, a chalk summoning circle on cracked concrete, a broken substation, drifting arcane glow

characters.charPrompt:
A character model-sheet drawing for a 2D television cartoon in the exact visual style of Samurai Jack (Genndy Tartakovsky): extremely simple large flat shapes, one thin uniform black outline, flat colors, minimal detail, angular geometry, plus Sin City heavy solid black shapes and a few stark white highlights. It must look like a cel from the show, NOT detailed anime or fantasy concept art.
CHARACTER: Interceptors, male human (Irish-Scottish heritage, Scottish), apparent age mid 40s. wiry and hard-jawed, medium size. Pose: wide fighting stance with the crowbar swung back over one shoulder. Expression: fierce, jaw set, one eyebrow cocked, as a minimal face. Design the silhouette first (heavy trapezoids, oversized fists and shoulders); the pose and the hero prop must read as a solid black shape.
SIMPLIFICATION BUDGET (the most important rule): HERO PROP, the one detailed object: ram-bar. SECOND ITEM, kept plain: tire-iron. COSTUME: only three big masses (main garment, legs, boots) as large flat angular polygons. Source costume notes, to be CUT by about 70% and used only as a loose guide: hard-jawed human driver in a spiked black leather jacket, driving gloves, goggles pushed up on the forehead and boots, one hand gripping a heavy tire-iron, the other fist wrapped in a spiked knuckle-duster.
HOW TO DRAW IT: FIGURE: about 12 to 15 big shapes in total; OUTLINE: one thin, uniform-weight black line, no sketchy or variable-weight lines; SHADING: each material is one flat color plus at most one flat darker shadow shape; no shine, no soft shading, no rim light; FACE: minimal; eyes are two simple geometric shapes (almond, slit or dot) under one brow line, nose one angular line, mouth one line; no eyelashes, eye highlights, iris detail or skin shading; HAIR and FUR: two to four big solid pointed shapes, never strands, braids, curls or texture; FABRIC: large flat planes with straight or sharply angled edges and at most three big creases; no ragged hems, ribbon streamers, patterns, embroidery, trim bands, tassels, stitching, studs or rows of buckles; METAL and GEAR: plain solid shapes in flat grey, black or an assigned color; chains are one thick plain line; no engraving or gold shading; HANDS and FEET: simple blocky shapes; at most ONE repeated graphic symbol on the whole figure; clear negative space between limbs, prop and body.
COLOR (exact hex, flat fills): main #d00000 about 60%, on the largest garment, armor, fur-marking or body areas; secondary #f8f9fa about 30%, on trim, sash, straps, secondary garment pieces and held gear; pop #ffba08 about 10%, on the eyes, the Armored coupe and one small magical detail. Also allowed: black, white, neutral grey and one flat simplified skin, fur or species tone. No cream, tan, brass, gold or silver unless assigned. Never use #d9a521 (background only).
NEVER: photorealism, 3D or CGI, painterly or watercolor texture, detailed anime rendering, airbrushing, gradients, glow or bloom or lens flare (a glow is a flat solid shape), fabric texture, tiny decorations, individual hairs, realistic reflections, generic fantasy concept art.
SELF-CHECK before finishing: Is it recognizable filled solid black? Could an animator redraw it with a few large shapes? Readable as a thumbnail? Colors flat and separated by the outline? Distinctive without surface detail? If any answer is no, remove detail until all are yes.
COMPOSITION: one full-body figure, head to toe, nothing cropped, clear margin, centered, all shapes fully filled and opaque. True transparent background: no floor, shadow, scene, checkerboard, border or text. 3:4 portrait. Bruiser, combat, Human people, mature dark-age tone, no nudity, no gore.
characters.bgPrompt:
Heavily stippled charcoal and ink illustration on toned paper, a graphic-novel panel with Sin City contrast: dense dotted halftone and grainy ink texture over every surface, bold black ink linework, hand-drawn painted shapes. NOT photorealistic, NOT a 3D render, NOT smooth digital concept art, no lens flare. 16:9 landscape, 1980s post-apocalyptic neo-retro cyberpunk dark-age mood.
SCENE: a barricaded highway-overpass settlement: stacked shipping containers, riveted gates, a tall radio mast, sodium street lamps, rain-slick asphalt, tarp banners. An empty environment for Interceptors with no people, creatures, figures, silhouettes or text. Midground: an armored coupe with a spiked ram-bar and one glowing amber headlight parked at the lower-right, stacks of spare tires. Foreground: a fuel drum, a hand-painted convoy banner, plus wet ground reflecting light. Large props the character cannot wear or carry live here, never in a hand.
COLOR (most important): a GOLD-washed painting. The people color #d9a521 washes about 65% of the image across sky, fog, ground, walls and haze. Accents about 20%, clearly visible: main #d00000 for the biggest glowing sources and surfaces, secondary #f8f9fa for medium panels, banners and lights, pop #ffba08 for small sparks and glints, reflected on the ground. Black and white for ink linework, deep shadows and highlights.
COMPOSITION: horizon at one-third height, a moon upper-left, open empty space in the lower center where the character will stand, props pushed to the left and right edges.
